name: Stepper Motor Calculator
blurb: pulse frequency and torque from step angle, microstepping and speed
intro: Turns a speed (rpm, or mm/s through a lead screw or belt) into the STEP pulse frequency and resolution, and estimates the torque left at that speed from a first-order phase model: the supply must drive the rated current through the winding's resistance, inductance and back-EMF. The datasheet pull-out curve always wins over this estimate.

inputs.label: Travel per revolution
inputs.help: Lead screw lead (pitch × starts), or belt pitch × pulley teeth (GT2 × 20 T = 40 mm).

inputs.label: Holding torque
inputs.help: Datasheet value, both phases at rated current.

inputs.label: Driver current setting
inputs.help: Peak phase current the driver regulates to.

inputs.label: Max step input rate
inputs.help: Driver or MCU limit, e.g. A4988 ≈ 500 kHz (1 µs high + 1 µs low); leave blank to skip.

examples.title: NEMA 17 on a T8 lead screw at 50 mm/s, 1/16 steps, 24 V
NEMA 23 direct drive at 600 rpm, 1/8 steps, 36 V

usage: Give the full-step angle in degrees, the microstep divisor (1-256), the speed either as rpm (motion=rotary) or as mm/s with the travel per revolution in mm (motion=linear), and the motor data: holding torque N·m, rated and driver current A, inductance mH, resistance Ω, supply V, and optionally the max step rate in kHz. It returns the STEP frequency, step period, steps/rev and steps/mm, microstep resolution, the estimated torque at that speed, the corner speed and a torque-speed curve. Use it to size a step timer or check a motor/supply choice before the datasheet curve is at hand.
sources: Phase voltage model V = |I(R + jωL) + E| per winding, electrical frequency = full-step rate / 4 for a 2-phase hybrid motor (standard first-order stepper model, e.g. Oriental Motor technical reference 'Stepping motor characteristics')
Incremental microstep torque T·sin(90°/n): Faulhaber/MICROMO application note 'Microstepping myths and realities'
Back-EMF constant estimated as holding torque / (√2 · rated current) per phase (rule of thumb)
